description: Issue #839: when a program contains BOTH kinds of declaration-slot collision, BOTH are reported, and the one first in SOURCE ORDER is reported first. Here a duplicate `tally` on line 4 precedes a built-in `define forward` on line 7, and that is the order the findings arrive in. Issue #815 changed which stage decides this: phase-1 registration still halts at the first collision, but the check that now runs before it sees the whole program, so the later `ol-reserved-word` IS produced — what stayed worth pinning is the ORDER, because it is the order a learner reads. It remains deliberately separate from the *priority* property (`ol-reserved-word` beats `ol-duplicate-definition` when ONE name is both). The mirror program — the `define forward` block first, then the duplicated `tally` — leads with `ol-reserved-word`; it is pinned as a unit test (`execute-declaration-slots.test.mjs`, "the first collision reported is the first in source order, whichever code it carries") rather than as a second fixture, since the two differ only in block order. Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists, but it runs only under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — NOT in this fixture, which is checked — and when it does run it is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why the runtime's copy never appears beside the check's. So nothing here observes that copy, and reading this fixture as evidence for it would be a mistake: measured, a runtime guard can be deleted outright with the whole conformance corpus still green, because the surviving report is the check's either way. What the runtime copy uniquely contributes is that the run STOPS at the fault, which is written in the event stream rather than in the diagnostics and is pinned by `packages/runtime/src/runtime-guards-halt.test.mjs`. The other findings recorded here are independent faults in the same program, each reported once.
